newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late rubber falls despite Tokyo rises.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late rubber falls despite Tokyo rises.

text.p: Indonesian benchmark tyre-grade SIR20 offer prices edged down in slow late trading on Wednesday on continued weak demand, dealers said.
"The falls had been expected after very slow demand since late last week. Some dealers are heard lowering their offer prices to 55.50 in Jambi, but no deals were done," one dealer said.

Dealers said SIR20 offer prices for October/November deliveries edged down 0.50-0.75 cents/lb to 56.25-56.75 U.S. cents/lb fob Medan and to 56.00-56.50 cents fob Palembang, Surabaya and Padang, and to 55.50-56.25 cents fob Jambi and Pontianak.
Dealers said demand was so weak, despite rises in the Tokyo rubber market, and very few enquiries were heard.
They said reports that the Maritime Union of Australia's would impose bans on Indonesian cargo and shipping due to human rights issues was unlikely to have much impact on prices.
Indonesia exported around 15,000 tonnes of rubber to Australia in 1994, or less than two percent of its total exports.
Export figures for 1995 were not available.
High amoniac grade latex with 60 percent dry rubber content was last traded at 2,230 rupiah/kg against the previous 2,250 rupiah in Bandung and Tangerang, dealers said.
